correctness.rationale: The A4 irreducibles have dimensions 1,1,1,3. The condition sigma(f)=3 gives only all three one-dimensional Fourier blocks active (f factors through A4/V4 with support multiple four) or exactly one rank-one 3x3 block (f(g)=u* rho(g)v). For the 3D tetrahedral signed-permutation representation, each of the three V4 cosets gives four sign combinations of coefficients a1,a2,a3. If all coordinates of u and v are nonzero, the four signed sums in each coset have at most one zero, so total support>=9. If some coordinate vanishes, each coset has a zero a_j and four values split into opposite pairs, yielding an even number of nonzeros globally. The general uncertainty inequality |supp(f)|sigma(f)>=12 then excludes sizes below 4. Thus 5 and 7 impossible. Seven explicit integer pairs of vectors actually give support sizes 4,6,8,9,10,11,12; independent exact direct signed-permutation evaluation reproduced every count. Source checker and Schur orthogonality identities were inspected. This proves exclusions over arbitrary complex coefficients; the finite integer grid was not treated as exhaustive.
